history.summary: Small Shiva temple at Narasipura, Hosadurga taluk, famous for the 'wishing well' Ganga Kola / Udbhava Ganga - a never-drying tank behind the garbhagriha whose milky-white water (halu = milk in Kannada) is said to come from Kashi. For a Rs 25 token, devotees pray and wait: auspicious items (banana, bangles, dates, raisins) surfacing from the water mean a wish will be fulfilled, while charcoal is a bad omen; priests interpret each item. Legend: during vanavasa, Rama worshipped a swayambhu linga here; the Ganga sprang up as a fountain of milk; Valmiki installed Ganga Mata above the Ganga Kola. Claimed to be one of Karnataka's Pancha Kashi Kshetras (UNVERIFIED). Architecture dated 14th-century Hoysala by one source (UNVERIFIED).

name: Halu Rameshwara Temple
town_description: CSV town 'Chitradurga' corrected: the temple is at Narasipura village in Hosadurga taluk of Chitradurga district (PIN 577527), about 12 km from Hosadurga and roughly 50-52 km from Chitradurga town. It is reached through agricultural country of arecanut and coconut plantations. The village is known almost solely for the Halu Rameshwara temple; coordinates above are geocoded to Narasipura village (approximate).

travel.railway: Chikjajur Junction and Chitradurga Railway Station are the nearest (verify)
travel.road: KSRTC/private buses to Hosadurga from Bengaluru, Mysuru and Chitradurga; ~12 km local transport from Hosadurga
